newsitem.title: GREECE: Ecu/drachma firms, rates rangebound in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Ecu/drachma firms, rates rangebound in late trade.

text.p: Ecu/drachma was trading around 303.26/31, above Monday's fix at 303.24, with money rates and implied forex forward drachma rates showing an upward bias.
But money rates were mostly still locked in the 13-13.50 percent range, traders said.
"Depos and implied forex forward rates are holding at a slightly higher level but still trading between 13-13.50 percent throughout the spectrum," said a trader at a foreign bank.
The central bank injected overnight liquidity at an unchanged 13.40 percent.
Ecu/drachma firmed on expressed interest to buy 40 to 50 million ecus by a Greek bank.
Dealers said they expected the ecu to strengthen against the drachma as the year-end approached.
The central bank has announced that it aims at a broadly stable ecu/drachma rate in 1996, which has been interpreted by the market as landing in the wider 304-308 range by year-end.
The forex outflows accompanying the squaring of ecu/drachma positions does not worry the central bank, which wants to discourage speculative inflows and rein in money supply.

Greece will auction about 200 billion drachmas worth of seven-year FRNs with the first coupon at 13.40 percent, the 12-month T-bill rate set at 12 percent and the spread at 10 basis points on November 22.

It will also auction 100 billion drachmas of three-year, 11-percent coupon bonds on November 12. Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis said last week that a five-year bond would be auctioned, but the ministry appears to have changed its mind.
The mark was quoted at 157.98/03 drachmas from Monday's 157.950 fix, the dollar at 237.79/89 drachmas from 237.940 and the Ecu at 303.27/37 from 303.080 drachmas.
